name: hdr-linux
note: Linux's HDR output, made whatever the desktop (XBE_HDR_FORCE=1: the desktop's HDR taken as on), its frame's brightness measured (XBE_HDR_STATS, read back as HDR10's PQ code values): the HDR10 back buffers on, the pause menu's white at the scene brightness set (200 nits, then 300), and off and on again with the setting. Windows on an HDR display measures the same frames alike (max 200 nits at 200). Without an HDR desktop (WSL's X11) the window shows the HDR10 picture as SDR: the screen path itself (an HDR10 swap chain on a desktop in HDR) is checked on a real one by hand.

expect: found(runlog, r'hdr: the display is HDR')

steps.until: room == 0 and player.active and not loading

steps.note: the pause menu's white at 200 nits
expect: any(185 <= float(l.split('max ')[1].split(' nits')[0]) <= 215 for l in found(log, r'hdr: frame'))
any(280 <= float(l.split('max ')[1].split(' nits')[0]) <= 320 for l in found(log, r'hdr: frame'))
